writes.rule: Per subtopic seen: pMastery 0.7 if right at D2/D3, 0.55 if right at D1, 0.25 if wrong; level L0-L3 from the ladder step reached
Prerequisite-gap index = 100 x weighted misses / weighted items seen in slots 1-4, averaged over groups
Groups with the highest Part A percent (top 1-2, only if >= 65%)
Groups with the lowest Part A percent (bottom 1-2, only if < 65%)
Calibration = 1 - mean |confidence/5 - correct| over Part A (feeds the first MCI reading)
Highest difficulty answered correctly twice in a row: D1 low, D2 medium, D3 high
Verbal reasoning = percent of Part B verbal items right
Numerical reasoning = percent of Part B numerical items right
Abstract reasoning = percent of Part B abstract items right
Spatial reasoning = percent of Part B spatial items right
Logical deduction = percent right on Part B items tagged p65
Numeracy fluency = numerical percent scaled by speed (right answers under target time count 1.2x, max 100)
Processing speed = 100 x share of Part B items answered right within target seconds
RIASEC profile: each career-interest item scored 1-5; letter score = mean of its 2 items; top 3 letters form the code (e.g. IRC)

items.stem: A loan of 20 000 is taken at 10% simple interest per year. How much interest is due after 2 years?
A trader buys goods for 800 and sells them for 1 000. What is the profit?
items.markingKey: A. 200. Selling price - cost price

items.stem: Goods costing 1 200 are sold at a 25% profit. What is the selling price?
Something a borrower pledges to a lender as security for a loan is called
items.markingKey: C. collateral. The lender can sell it if the loan is not repaid

items.stem: Why do formal lenders such as banks usually charge less interest than informal moneylenders?
items.answer: They are regulated and can spread risk across many borrowers
options: They are regulated and can spread risk across many borrowers
items.markingKey: A. They are regulated and can spread risk across many borrowers. Regulation limits interest rates

items.stem: A family borrows from a moneylender at 5% per month. Roughly what annual rate is this?
items.markingKey: C. about 60% a year. 5 x 12 months

items.stem: A shop sold 12, 15, 9 and 14 items over four days. What is the mean daily sale?
Sales rose from 40 000 to 50 000. What is the percentage increase?
Monthly costs were 30, 30, 30 and 90 (thousands). Why is the median a better summary than the mean here?
items.answer: The single large value pulls the mean up
options: There are too few values for a mean
The single large value pulls the mean up
items.markingKey: D. The single large value pulls the mean up. Medians resist outliers

items.stem: The accounting equation is
items.markingKey: C. Assets = Liabilities + Capital. What the business owns is financed by others or the owner

items.stem: A business has assets of 90 000 and liabilities of 25 000. What is the capital?
The owner introduces 10 000 cash into the business. What happens to the equation?
items.answer: Assets and capital both rise by 10 000
options: Assets and capital both rise by 10 000
items.markingKey: C. Assets and capital both rise by 10 000. Both sides change equally

items.stem: An increase in an asset is recorded as a
items.markingKey: A. debit. Assets increase on the debit side

items.stem: Goods are bought on credit from Ravi. Which account is credited?
items.markingKey: A. Ravi's account. Ravi becomes a creditor

items.stem: Rent of 5 000 is paid by cheque. What is the double entry?
items.markingKey: A. Debit Rent, credit Bank. Expense increases, bank decreases

items.stem: Credit sales of goods are first recorded in the
items.markingKey: D. sales journal (sales day book). A book of prime entry

items.stem: Which book records both cash and bank receipts and payments?
items.markingKey: D. a two-column cash book. It acts as both a journal and a ledger

items.stem: A contra entry in a two-column cash book occurs when
items.answer: cash is deposited into or withdrawn from the bank
options: cash is deposited into or withdrawn from the bank
items.markingKey: D. cash is deposited into or withdrawn from the bank. Both sides are within the cash book

items.stem: A trial balance is prepared to
items.answer: check that total debits equal total credits
options: check that total debits equal total credits
items.markingKey: C. check that total debits equal total credits. An arithmetical check of the ledger

items.stem: Which error will NOT be revealed by a trial balance?
items.answer: An entry completely omitted from the books
options: An entry completely omitted from the books
A debit entered as 500 and credit as 50
A balance left out of the trial balance
items.markingKey: A. An entry completely omitted from the books. Errors of omission keep the totals equal

items.stem: Repairs to machinery of 3 000 were debited to the Machinery account. What type of error is this?
items.markingKey: C. error of principle. Revenue expenditure was treated as capital

items.stem: A bank and a hospital belong to which sector?
items.markingKey: A. tertiary (services). They provide services

items.stem: A company that owns or controls production in more than one country is a
items.markingKey: B. multinational corporation (MNC). Also called a TNC

items.stem: Why do MNCs often set up factories in countries with lower wages?
items.answer: To reduce production costs and stay competitive
options: To reduce production costs and stay competitive
items.markingKey: C. To reduce production costs and stay competitive. Cost advantage

items.stem: A product label must show its MRP in India. MRP stands for
items.markingKey: B. maximum retail price. Consumers cannot be charged more

items.stem: Why do consumers need protection laws?
items.answer: Sellers may know more than buyers and could mislead them
options: Sellers may know more than buyers and could mislead them
Shops are owned by the state
items.markingKey: C. Sellers may know more than buyers and could mislead them. Information gaps

items.stem: Fair-trade labelling mainly aims to
items.answer: guarantee producers in poorer countries a fair price
options: guarantee producers in poorer countries a fair price
items.markingKey: B. guarantee producers in poorer countries a fair price. Ethical trade

items.stem: Which indicator best measures average income in a country?
items.markingKey: A. GNI (or GDP) per capita. Income per person

items.stem: Why is HDI considered a broader measure of development than income alone?
items.answer: It also includes health and education
options: It also includes health and education
items.markingKey: C. It also includes health and education. Life expectancy, schooling and income

items.stem: Country A has higher income per head than B, but lower life expectancy and literacy. What does this suggest?
items.answer: Income alone does not show overall well-being
options: A is more developed in every way
B must be poorer in all respects
Income alone does not show overall well-being
items.markingKey: D. Income alone does not show overall well-being. Development is multi-dimensional

items.stem: A person who takes the risk of starting a business is an
items.markingKey: A. entrepreneur. They combine resources

items.stem: Which is an example of a secondary-sector business?
items.markingKey: A. a car factory. Manufacturing

items.stem: Why do many new businesses fail in their first years?
items.answer: Poor cash flow and a lack of experience or market research
options: Poor cash flow and a lack of experience or market research
items.markingKey: B. Poor cash flow and a lack of experience or market research. Cash and planning problems

items.stem: A business owned and run by one person is a
items.markingKey: C. sole proprietorship (sole trader). One owner

items.stem: What does limited liability mean?
items.answer: Owners can lose only what they invested
options: Owners can lose only what they invested
items.markingKey: C. Owners can lose only what they invested. Personal assets are protected

items.stem: Why might a growing partnership convert into a private limited company?
items.answer: To raise more capital and protect owners with limited liability
options: To raise more capital and protect owners with limited liability
items.markingKey: B. To raise more capital and protect owners with limited liability. Growth and risk

items.stem: The most common objective of a new small business is
items.markingKey: A. survival. It must first stay open

items.stem: A SMART objective must be
items.answer: specific, measurable, achievable, realistic and time-bound
options: specific, measurable, achievable, realistic and time-bound
items.markingKey: D. specific, measurable, achievable, realistic and time-bound. Clear targets

items.stem: Why might a social enterprise not aim to maximise profit?
items.answer: Its main aim is a social or environmental goal
options: It is owned by the government
It is not allowed to make any profit
Its main aim is a social or environmental goal
items.markingKey: D. Its main aim is a social or environmental goal. Profit supports the mission

items.stem: Which group is an internal stakeholder?
items.markingKey: B. employees. They are inside the business

items.stem: Why might local residents object to a new factory?
items.answer: Noise, traffic and pollution could affect them
options: Noise, traffic and pollution could affect them
items.markingKey: D. Noise, traffic and pollution could affect them. External costs

items.stem: Shareholders want higher dividends and workers want higher pay. This is an example of
items.markingKey: A. stakeholder conflict. Objectives clash

items.stem: Per capita income is
items.answer: total national income divided by population
options: total national income divided by population
items.markingKey: A. total national income divided by population. Average income

items.stem: Farming and mining are part of the
items.markingKey: A. primary sector. Natural resources

items.stem: As countries develop, the share of workers in the tertiary sector usually
items.markingKey: C. rises. Services grow

items.stem: Goods bought from other countries are
items.markingKey: B. imports. Coming in

items.stem: A tax on imported goods is a
items.markingKey: C. tariff. It makes imports dearer

items.stem: Why might cheaper imported toys harm small domestic toy makers?
items.answer: Consumers may switch to the cheaper imports
options: Consumers may switch to the cheaper imports
items.markingKey: D. Consumers may switch to the cheaper imports. Competition

items.stem: Money solves the problem of the double coincidence of wants because it
items.markingKey: A. is a medium of exchange. Barter needs matching wants

items.stem: Which is a likely effect of rising inequality?
items.answer: A larger gap between rich and poor households
options: A larger gap between rich and poor households
items.markingKey: C. A larger gap between rich and poor households. Distribution widens

items.stem: Why can easy access to cheap credit help poor rural families?
items.answer: They can invest in seeds or tools without falling into debt traps
options: They can invest in seeds or tools without falling into debt traps
items.markingKey: D. They can invest in seeds or tools without falling into debt traps. Formal credit is cheaper

items.stem: The basic economic problem arises because
items.answer: wants are unlimited but resources are scarce
options: wants are unlimited but resources are scarce
items.markingKey: A. wants are unlimited but resources are scarce. Scarcity forces choice

items.stem: The next best alternative given up when making a choice is the
items.markingKey: A. opportunity cost. Cost of the forgone option

items.stem: A point inside a production possibility frontier shows
items.markingKey: A. unemployed or inefficiently used resources. More could be produced

items.stem: The law of demand says that as price falls, quantity demanded
items.markingKey: A. rises. Other things equal

items.stem: A rise in income increases demand for a normal good. On a graph, this
items.answer: shifts the demand curve to the right
options: shifts the demand curve to the right
items.markingKey: B. shifts the demand curve to the right. A change in a non-price factor

items.stem: The price of tea rises. What happens to demand for coffee and for sugar?
items.answer: Coffee demand rises; sugar demand falls
options: Coffee demand rises; sugar demand falls
items.markingKey: C. Coffee demand rises; sugar demand falls. Coffee is a substitute, sugar a complement

items.stem: At equilibrium, quantity demanded
items.markingKey: C. equals quantity supplied. Market clears

items.stem: If price is below equilibrium there is
items.markingKey: C. excess demand (a shortage). Buyers want more than is offered

items.stem: A government sets a maximum rent below the equilibrium. What is the likely result?
items.markingKey: A. A shortage of rental housing. Price ceiling

items.stem: If demand is price elastic, a price rise causes
items.answer: a proportionately larger fall in quantity demanded
options: a proportionately larger fall in quantity demanded
items.markingKey: C. a proportionately larger fall in quantity demanded. PED > 1

items.stem: Price rises by 10% and quantity demanded falls by 5%. What is PED?
Why is demand for salt usually price inelastic?
items.answer: It is a necessity with few substitutes and a small share of income
options: It is a necessity with few substitutes and a small share of income
items.markingKey: A. It is a necessity with few substitutes and a small share of income. Determinants of PED

items.stem: Solve x² - 7x + 12 = 0.
What is sin 30°?
items.markingKey: B. 1/2. Standard value

items.stem: If tan θ = 3/4 and θ is acute, what is sin θ?
items.markingKey: B. 3/5. A 3-4-5 triangle

items.stem: What is the 10th term of 4, 7, 10, ...?
Which term of 5, 9, 13, ... is 81?
The sum of the first n odd numbers 1 + 3 + 5 + ... is
items.markingKey: B. n². Sum of an AP

items.stem: A coin is tossed and a die is rolled. What is P(head and a 6)?
A bag has 4 red and 6 blue balls. Two are drawn without replacement. What is P(both red)?
P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A and B) = 0.2. What is P(A or B)?
items.markingKey: A. 0.7. P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B)

items.stem: Write 45 000 in standard form.
items.markingKey: C. 4.5 x 10⁴. One digit before the decimal point

items.stem: What is log₁₀ 100 + log₁₀ 10?
A measurement of 5.0 m has an error of 0.2 m. What is the percentage error?
What is the 6th term of 2, 6, 18, ...?
A salary of 30 000 rises by 2 000 each year. What is it in year 5?
A town of 50 000 grows by 4% a year. Roughly what is its population after 3 years?
10 000 is invested at 6% compound interest a year. What is it worth after 2 years?
A car bought for 8 lakh depreciates 15% a year. Roughly what is it worth after 2 years?
Which is better for a saver: 8% compounded yearly or 8% compounded quarterly?
items.answer: Quarterly, because interest is added more often
options: Yearly, because there are fewer payments
They always give the same amount
Yearly, because the rate is the same
Quarterly, because interest is added more often
items.markingKey: D. Quarterly, because interest is added more often. Effective rate is higher

items.stem: A correlation coefficient of -0.9 shows
items.markingKey: C. a strong negative relationship. Close to -1

items.stem: Two data sets have the same mean, but A has a larger standard deviation. What does this mean?
items.markingKey: D. A is more spread out. Spread about the mean

items.stem: Ice-cream sales and drownings are strongly correlated. Why does this not prove one causes the other?
items.answer: Both may be caused by hot weather
options: Both may be caused by hot weather
items.markingKey: B. Both may be caused by hot weather. A third (lurking) variable

items.stem: What number comes next? 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ?
items.explanation: Each term is the sum of the two before it

items.stem: Money doubles in 6 years at a fixed compound rate. In how many years does it become 8 times?
Boys and girls in a class are in the ratio 3 : 5. After 6 more boys join, the ratio is 1 : 1. How many students were there at first?
One pipe fills a tank in 6 hours; another empties it in 9 hours. If both are open, how long does it take to fill the empty tank?
Which phrase is closest in meaning to 'ubiquitous'?
Author is to novel as composer is to ...
Some economists are writers. All writers are readers. Which statement must be true?
items.explanation: The economists who are writers are also readers

items.stem: Claim: 'Since the new study app launched, the school's test scores rose, so the app raised scores.' Which fact, if true, most weakens the claim?
options: The school also hired extra teachers at the same time
Students said they liked the app
items.answer: The school also hired extra teachers at the same time
items.explanation: Another change at the same time offers a different explanation

items.stem: What comes next? AZ, BY, CX, ?
items.explanation: First letters go forward, second letters go backward

items.stem: What comes next? 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, ?
Figures: shaded triangle, unshaded square, shaded pentagon, ... Each figure gains one side and the shading alternates. What is the next figure?
items.explanation: Six sides, and the shading switches back to unshaded

items.stem: What is the smaller angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 3:15?
items.explanation: The hour hand has moved a quarter of 30° past the 3

items.stem: From home you walk 4 km north and then 3 km east. How far are you from home in a straight line?

items.explanation: One at the centre of each face
